newsitem.title: FRANCE: Soros investment stirs up Moulinex.
newsitem.headline: Soros investment stirs up Moulinex.

text.p: George Soros's golden touch worked its magic on troubled French appliance maker Moulinex, whose stock rallied on Thursday after the Hungarian-born investor took a 5.5 percent stake.

Traders and analysts said they did not believe Soros's move signalled bid intentions, but the stock was up four percent at midday on the view that his interest in the company appeared to validate its recently unveiled recovery programme.
The stock was up 4.30 francs at 115.40 francs at 1245 GMT.
"People think highly of Soros, and he has followers," a trader said.
The shrewd 66-year-old financier has built a multi-billion dollar fortune in the world financial markets over the past 27 years and is also renowned for his philanthropy.
Moulinex refused to comment on his investment, which was announced on Wednesday evening by the French stockmarkets association SBF.

The SBF said three firms he controls -- Quantum Partners LDC, Geosor Corp and Lupa Family Partners LP -- had bought a combined 5.48 percent stake on November 12 representing 1.55 million Moulinex shares and 4.39 percent of the voting rights.

A source close to Moulinex said the purchase was not perceived as a takeover move, and he added that the shareholder structure -- a typically French cascade of holding companies -- provided some protection from unwelcome advances.
Moulinex's biggest shareholder, Euris, holds 33 percent of Financiere Moulinex, which in turn controls 28 percent of Moulinex and 41 percent of the voting rights.
"It would be very difficult to launch a buyout bid, and we don't have the feeling that that's what this is. He wouldn't have any interest in taking over Moulinex," the source said.
"But Moulinex is a globally recognised brand, Krupps (its coffee maker line) is known in Germany and the United States, and this is an industry in which the French are good," he added.

Chairman Pierre Blayau unveiled a plan in June to revive the company, which lost money in each of the last four years, and he has strong experience in retailing, the source said. "We think Soros has made the same analysis."
The share has gained 40 percent since the restructuring plan was announced.
Analyst Lilyane Dufroid Reynaud at brokerage SGE Delahaye said she believed Soros viewed Moulinex as a good investment.
"Soros looks for shares with potential, and he estimates that, at that price, the stock is worth it," she said. She said the stock could rise substantially more if the restructuring plan succeeded.
Blayau announced the plan, which entails job cuts of more than 20 percent and two plant closures in France, in June after the group reported a loss for 1995/96 of 720 million francs ($142 million).
He had been installed at Moulinex earlier in the year by leading shareholder Euris, which was reported to be impatient with the recovery pace under the previous management.

Analysts say the company, which has drifted since the death in 1988 of its founder Jean Mantelet, is hobbled by high labour costs, old and inefficient factories and a dated product line in an increasingly competitive industry.
Although investors applauded the recovery plan, the management has drawn fire from workers and politicians for what is viewed as an extremely brutal solution by French standards.
The company's staff committee, which includes worker representatives, will examine the plan on December 6 in what promises to be a heated debate.
Moulinex's successful French rival, appliance manufacturer SEB, got a strong boost on Thursday from Soros's investment in Moulinex, rising 2.39 percent to 1,027 francs.
"SEB is up because people feel it has better fundamentals," a trader said.
($1=5.070 French Franc)
